comments.text:
What if skipping a vote was a literal crime, but the penalty came with a side of onions and BBQ? 
While the Australian government was busy fighting the Emu War in 1932 as mentioned at 18-46, they were also enforcing a very unique law - mandatory voting. Since 1924, every citizen over 18 is legally required to vote or face a financial fine. Because this brings the entire population to the polls, it birthed a legendary national tradition called the "Democracy Sausage." At every polling station, charities set up grills to sell sausages in bread, turning a serious legal obligation into a massive nationwide barbecue festival. It is a fascinating addition to the video's theme of isolation: while other nations struggle with turnout, Australia has turned its legal system into a unique social celebration! 😱
